concepts.def: Sudden public fear about a group

walkthroughs.body_html:
A moral panic = sudden public fear that a group is wrecking society.

News reports inflate small events. People demand action.

In 1972 sociologist Stanley Cohen studied 1964 clashes between Mods and Rockers at UK seaside towns.

News papers blew up small scuffles into national fear — turning the youths into 'folk devils'.

Modern panics:

  • Hoodies, knife crime.
  • TikTok challenges.
  • Gaming and screen time.

Some danger is real, but media often exaggerates. Always check the data. 🔍
